claim: For the closed generalized three-qubit W family \(|W(p,q,r)\rangle=\sqrt p\,|100\rangle+\sqrt q\,|010\rangle+\sqrt r\,|001\rangle\), where \(p,q,r\ge 0\) and \(p+q+r=1\), let \(\omega\) be the squared maximal product overlap and let \(P_{\rm PT}\) be the two-copy product-test acceptance probability. The feasible overlap range is \([4/9,1]\). For \(4/9\le\omega\le1/2\), define \(T(\omega)=[9\omega-4+3\sqrt{\omega(9\omega-4)}]/2\). Then the exact W-family frontier is \(P_{\rm PT}\le(8+T(\omega)^2)/12\), with equality exactly, up to permutation and local phases, at probabilities \(((1-T)/3,(2+T)/6,(2+T)/6)\). For \(1/2\le\omega\le1\), the exact frontier is \(P_{\rm PT}\le1-\omega+\omega^2\), with equality exactly, up to permutation and local phases, at \((\omega,1-\omega,0)\). On \([4/9,1/2)\) this W-family frontier is strictly below the dimension-free product-test curve \(1-2\omega+3\omega^2\); if \(t=T(\omega)\), the gap is \((1-t)(t+2)(5t^2+5t+2)/[108(1+t)^2]\), ranging from \(1/27\) at the W state to \(0\) at \(\omega=1/2\).

correctness.rationale: The claim follows from the exact product-test purity identity, the inspected generalized-W product-overlap theorem, an explicit fixed-second-moment trigonometric parametrization whose product is minimized at the one-small/two-equal triple, monotonic inversion of the induced overlap bound, and an elementary high-overlap convexity step. Equality conditions and endpoints are tracked throughout.
risks: The generalized-W overlap formula is external; a defect in that published theorem would affect the result. The finite checker is corroborative and not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The result is a natural complete classification on the canonical generalized W family, directly addressing a fixed-dimension obstruction highlighted by a 2026 product-test theorem. It identifies all equality states, produces an explicit strict gap from the dimension-free curve throughout the nontrivial low-overlap interval, and anchors that gap at the globally extremal W state.
risks: The theorem is a family-level benchmark rather than the final fixed-local-dimension three-qubit solution; its value lies in the exact canonical subproblem and obstruction it quantifies.
